name: Stewing Beef Casserole
description: A hearty beef casserole with vegetables, slow-cooked at a low temperature for tender results.

recipeInstructions.text: Mix all ingredients lightly in a bowl.
Transfer the mixture to a casserole dish or roasting pan and cover tightly.
Bake at 250°F for 4 hours without uncovering.

keywords: beef casserole, slow-cooked stew, comfort food

_similar.name: Noodles with Hamburg
_similar.description: A hearty casserole featuring ground hamburger, macaroni, and a blend of vegetables and cheese.

recipeInstructions.text: In a frying pan, brown the hamburger with celery and onions (if using). Drain excess fat.
Add garlic powder, oregano, salt, tomato soup, corn, and canned tomatoes to the browned hamburger mixture. Stir to combine.
Simmer the mixture slowly for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook macaroni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
Combine the cooked macaroni with the hamburger and sauce mixture. Stir well.
If using cheese, heat it until melted and mix into the noodle and hamburger mixture.
Serve hot.

_similar.keywords: hamburger casserole, noodle dish, comfort food

_similar.name: Cabbage Rolls
_similar.description: Traditional cabbage rolls filled with a savory mixture of ground pork, beef, and rice, simmered in tomato juice.

recipeInstructions.text: Boil the cabbage head for 10 minutes to soften the leaves. Drain and let cool.
Chop the onion and fry in lard for 10 minutes until softened.
Mix the cooked onion and lard with ground pork, ground beef, rice, salt, and pepper until well combined.
Peel off cabbage leaves and cut out the thick stem. Place about 1 tablespoon of the meat mixture in the center of each leaf, fold the sides, and roll into a neat package.
Line the bottom of a large pot with a layer of cabbage leaves to prevent burning.
Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot, layering them as needed.
Pour the tomato juice over the cabbage rolls, ensuring they are mostly covered.
Bring the tomato juice to a simmer, then reduce heat and let cook for the entire afternoon (approximately 3 hours).

_similar.keywords: cabbage rolls, stuffed cabbage, ground meat, comfort food

_similar.name: Shepherd's Pie
_similar.description: A classic shepherd's pie made with ground beef, mixed vegetables, and topped with mashed potatoes.

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the ground beef in an electric skillet. Drain excess fat.
Add onion soup mix, frozen vegetables, beef cube, salt, and pepper. Simmer for approximately 10 minutes.
Pour the mixture into a 6-cup (1.5 L) casserole dish or square baking dish.
Top with mashed potatoes and sprinkle with paprika if desired.
Bake at 400°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are firm and golden brown.
Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

_similar.keywords: shepherd's pie, ground beef, mashed potatoes, casserole

_similar.name: Beef Porcupines
_similar.description: Baked meatballs with rice, served in a tangy tomato-based sauce.

recipeInstructions.text: Mix ground beef, rice, onion, mustard, chili powder, salt, allspice, brown sugar, pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and paprika. Form into balls.
Place meatballs in a baking dish.
Combine tomato soup and hot water to make the sauce. Pour over meatballs.
Cover and bake at 350°F for 1 hour.

_similar.name: Turkey A La King
_similar.description: A creamy turkey dish made with mushrooms, celery, and green pepper, served over toast or rice.

recipeInstructions.text: In a skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add mushrooms, onion, celery, and green pepper. Cook until vegetables are tender.
Remove vegetables from skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside.
In the same skillet, blend flour into the butter to make a roux. Gradually add chicken broth and milk, stirring constantly.
Bring mixture to a boil and cook for 2 minutes, or until it thickens.
Add reserved turkey and vegetables to the sauce. Heat through.
Serve over hot toast, biscuits, or rice.

_similar.keywords: turkey a la king, creamy turkey, mushrooms, celery, green pepper
